recipe.title: Carrot, cheddar and thyme scones
recipe.intro: October carrots are sweet and plentiful, and grated into a cheese scone they keep it soft and golden. Just right for an after-school snack on a chilly afternoon.
steps: Heat the oven to 200C fan, 220C conventional, and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Mix the flour, baking powder, salt and pepper in a large bowl. Rub in the butter with your fingertips until it looks like fine breadcrumbs.
Stir in the carrots, most of the cheddar and the thyme, keeping a small handful of cheese back for the tops.
Beat the egg into the milk in a jug and set aside 1 tbsp for glazing. Pour the rest into the bowl and mix with a fork into a soft, slightly sticky dough.
Tip onto a floured surface and pat gently into a round about 3cm thick. Don't knead it, or the scones will be tough. Cut into 8 wedges.
Space the wedges out on the tray, brush with the saved egg and milk and scatter over the remaining cheese.
Bake for 15 to 18 minutes until risen, deep golden and hollow sounding underneath. Cool for 5 minutes and eat warm with butter.
recipe.tip: They keep for 2 days in a tin and freeze well. Warm them through in a low oven for 5 minutes.
